taxonomy.title: CHC taxonomy (Schneider & McGrew, 2018)
taxonomy.source: Schneider, W. J., & McGrew, K. S. (2018). The Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory of cognitive abilities. In D. P. Flanagan & E. M. McDonough (Eds.), Contemporary intellectual assessment: Theories, tests, and issues (4th ed.). Guilford Press.
taxonomy.source_text: Schneider, W. J., & McGrew, K. S. (2017). CHC broad and narrow ability definitions (07-20-17). Institute for Applied Psychometrics. http://www.iapsych.com/chcdefs.pdf -- the authors' abstract of the 2018 chapter. Every name, broad description, and narrow definition in this file is transcribed verbatim from it
taxonomy.lineage: Schneider, W. J., & McGrew, K. S. (2013). The Cattell-Horn-Carroll (CHC) model of intelligence v2.2: A visual tour and summary. Institute for Applied Psychometrics.
taxonomy.scope_note: Restricted to the 13 broad abilities the 2017 sheet does not mark as tentative (Gf, Gwm, Gl, Gv, Ga, Gc, Gkn, Grw, Gq, Gr, Gs, Gt, Gps). The five broad abilities the sheet's legend marks as "other tentatively identified broad abilities" (red: Gp, Go, Gh, Gk, Gei) are excluded with their narrow abilities. Narrow abilities the sheet marks as tentative (italic code: Gf-RE Reasoning speed, Gf-RP Piagetian reasoning) are excluded as well. Abilities the source lists under more than one broad ability are kept once, under the parent where the source gives their full definition: Reading speed (RS) and Writing speed (WS) under Grw, Perceptual speed (P) under Gs; the other listings (Gs-RS, Gs-WS, Gps-WS, and the Gv-P pointer) are omitted, and cross-listing is not represented.  Working memory capacity (Wc) is omitted because the source states it is "technically not a narrow ability. Result: 13 broad, 71 narrow abilities.
taxonomy.flags_note: `major` transcribes the source's typography: bold narrow code = major ability (true), regular = minor (false); where every code under a broad ability is regular (here Gt and Gps), the source means insufficient data to classify, recorded as null.
taxonomy.code_note: Codes are as in the source except Musical discrimination and judgment, which the source writes "U1 U9" and this file writes U1U9 so that the uid Ga-U1U9 is filesystem-safe.

project_annotations.title: CHC folk-vocabulary project annotations
project_annotations.scope: Everything this project added to the published CHC taxonomy: per-narrow-ability discriminator glosses and folk seed sentences (keyed by uid = <broad>-<narrow>), and a per-broad-ability conceptual grouping. Joined with the taxonomy by src/data/inventory.py.
project_annotations.history: Version 1.0 (2026-09-30) accompanies the revised taxonomy transcribed from Schneider & McGrew (2017/2018). It was carried over from data/raw/chc_ability_inventory.json (file version 2.6, git history), keeping the seeds and discriminators of the 69 abilities that remain. Dropped with the taxonomy revision: Gc-OP, Gkn-A5, Gkn-BC (not in the 2018 revision), the cross-listings Gs-RS, Gs-WS, Gps-WS, and every narrow ability of the tentative broad abilities (Go-OM; Gp-AI, P1, P2, P3, P4, P6, P7, P8).
project_annotations.seeds_note: `seeds` holds 10 folk-description seed sentences per narrow ability, the set revised after the 2026-06-10 top-100 retrieval audit: per ability the revision purged the homographs and idioms identified as leak sources, re-anchored on the recommended folk register (lay self-report, deficit poles, niche communities), and carries the discriminator. The original LLM-authored set it replaced (`seeds_v2.5` in the pre-revision inventory) was dropped from this file on 2026-09-30 and survives in git history. Retrieval, classifier training, filtering, and the RQ3 seed condition all read `seeds`; there is no fallback, and the loader refuses an ability without seeds.
project_annotations.conceptual_group_note: Project grouping, adapted from Schneider and McGrew's (2012) functional-conceptual framework and not taken verbatim from it. Labels differ from the source (source Memory -> Memory and Efficiency, General Speed -> Speed and Efficiency; Gf, ungrouped in the source, -> Reasoning).

broad_abilities.name: Fluid reasoning
broad_abilities.description: The use of deliberate and controlled procedures (often requiring focused attention) to solve novel "on the spot" problems that cannot be solved by using previously learned habits, schemas, and scripts.

narrow_abilities.name: Induction
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to observe a phenomenon and discover the underlying principles or rules that determine its behavior. This ability is also known as rule inference.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs RG — infers an unknown rule from observed instances, rather than applying a rule already given.
seeds: After watching the machine jam a few times, she figured out on her own what kept setting it off.
He never touches the instructions — he plays a couple of rounds and just works out how the thing must work underneath.
Give her a handful of examples and she'll tell you what they all secretly have in common.
Nobody ever explained the system to him, but after a week he'd pieced together exactly how the place really ran.
She's the type who notices the same odd thing keeps happening every few weeks, then works backward to why.
After seeing it happen a dozen times, she worked out the pattern behind why it kept turning out that way.
She studied case after case until she could state the hidden rule that tied them all together.
He kept quiet track of when the dog got anxious and eventually cracked what was setting it off.
Shown a run of figures, she works out the rule that decides which number comes next.
Nobody spelled it out, but he picked up on the unspoken logic in how the team kept making its calls.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: The ability to observe a phenomenon and discover the underlying principles or rules that determine its behavior. Also known as rule inference.

narrow_abilities.name: General sequential reasoning
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to reason logically using known premises and principles. This ability is also known as deductive reasoning or rule application.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs I — chains given premises step-by-step to a forced conclusion rather than discovering the rule; vs RQ — non-quantitative.
seeds: Set out the conditions of a logic puzzle and he steps through them one at a time to the single answer they force.
She laid the case out link by link until there was no way left to argue with where it ended up.
Give him 'this is true and that's true,' and he'll tell you exactly what has to follow — no leaps, just steps.
She noticed the conclusion didn't actually follow from the steps that led up to it.
Give her a grid of clues about who sat where and she deduces each placement from the ones already pinned down.
Give him the constraints and he'll work out who must have been where, ruling out the impossible ones one at a time.
She worked out the seating just from the clues — if A sits here, then B can't, and on down the line.
He never skips a step; from the given premises he carries it straight through to the one conclusion they allow.
From the rules of the game alone she worked out the one move that couldn't lose.
He took the points everyone had already accepted and walked them, step by step, to where they were forced to land.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: The ability to reason logically using known premises and principles. Also known as deductive reasoning or rule application.

narrow_abilities.name: Quantitative reasoning
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to reason with quantities, mathematical relations, and operators.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs KM/A3 (Gq) — reasons about quantitative relationships on a novel problem rather than recalling math facts or doing graded computation; vs N (Gs) — reasoning, not calculation speed.
seeds: He reads a word problem and instantly sees which amounts hang on which, before he's touched a single number.
She can work out in her head roughly how much longer the trip takes if you ease off the speed a little.
Give him a speed and a distance and he'll get to the time in his head, without writing a thing down.
She figured out how to share the work fairly by thinking through the proportions, no arithmetic needed.
Hand him an unfamiliar puzzle about amounts and he works out from scratch how they have to fit together.
She reasoned that if the tank was draining that fast it couldn't possibly last the trip — and it didn't.
He can tell you which of two recipes ends up richer once you see how the ingredient ratios stack up.
From how the readings were spaced he worked out what the rate of change had to be.
He thinks naturally about how quantities scale — stretch one and what happens to the rest — and it just makes sense to him.
She worked out how many batches she'd need by thinking the proportions through, not by guessing.

broad_abilities.name: Comprehension-knowledge
broad_abilities.description: The ability to comprehend and communicate culturally-valued knowledge. Gc includes the depth and breadth of both declarative and procedural knowledge and skills such as language, words, and general knowledge developed through experience, learning and acculturation.

narrow_abilities.name: Language Development
narrow_abilities.definition: An intermediate stratum ability to comprehend and communicate using language. The general understanding of spoken language at the level of words, idioms, and sentences.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs VL — broad comprehension of words/idioms/sentences, not single-word definitions; vs LS — not channel-specific to listening.
seeds: Even as a little kid she followed complicated sentences the adults assumed would sail right over her head.
He takes in the meaning of an idiom or a turn of phrase the first time he hears it, and uses it right back.
She can follow a long, winding explanation without ever losing the thread of it.
He picks up what an unfamiliar expression means just from the way it sits in the sentence.
She's always had an easy command of words — explaining, understanding, making herself plain.
He caught the wording of the joke instantly while the rest of us were still untangling it.
She handles the little subtleties of phrasing that trip most people up.
From early on he could say exactly what he meant and catch exactly what other people meant.
She grasps the full meaning of a complicated remark, not just the words themselves.
He follows what a dense, many-claused sentence is really saying without it tripping him up.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: An intermediate stratum ability reflecting the general understanding of spoken language at the level of words, idioms, and sentences. The ability to comprehend and communicate using language.

narrow_abilities.name: Lexical knowledge
narrow_abilities.definition: The knowledge of the definitions of words and the concepts that underlie them. Vocabulary knowledge.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs LD — knowledge of what individual words mean; vs K0 — words, not world facts.
seeds: She always has the exact word for the thing — even the obscure ones nobody else can come up with.
He can tell you the precise difference in meaning between two near-synonyms most people use interchangeably.
Her word-stock is enormous; a crossword has never once stumped her on a meaning.
He knew what that ten-dollar word meant off the top of his head, and used it dead right.
She collects words the way other people collect stamps, and she knows what every one of them means.
Whatever the word, he can give you its exact definition without hesitating.
She reaches for the perfect, specific word while the rest of us settle for 'thing.'
He came up with that subtle word that captured it exactly — the one no one else could land on.
Her sense of what words actually mean is razor sharp; she'll flag a misused one on the spot.
He knows the fine shades of meaning that separate one word from its close cousins.

narrow_abilities.name: General (verbal) information
narrow_abilities.definition: The breadth and depth of knowledge that one’s culture deems essential, practical, or worthwhile for everyone to know.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs VL — stored common-cultural facts, not word meanings; vs Gkn — common, not specialized knowledge.
seeds: She's a walking encyclopedia of the stuff everyone's sort of supposed to know.
He always knows which country borders which, who wrote what, when things happened.
Ask her any general-knowledge question and odds are she just knows the answer.
He's the one you want on your pub-quiz team for all the everyday facts.
She's got this broad store of common knowledge that makes her unbeatable at trivia.
He just seems to know things — capitals, inventions, who did what when, all of it.
She holds onto everyday facts that other people lose track of soon after learning them.
He can rattle off the basics of almost any common topic that comes up.
Her general knowledge is wide — a little about nearly everything worth knowing.
He always knows the well-known facts that surface in ordinary conversation.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: The breadth and depth of knowledge that one's culture deems essential, practical, and worthwhile for everyone to know.

narrow_abilities.name: Listening ability
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to understand speech. This ability starts with comprehending single words and increases to long complex verbal statements.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs LD — comprehension specifically by ear; vs UR (Ga) — grasping meaning, not merely hearing a degraded signal.
seeds: She can follow a dense lecture by ear alone and come away knowing exactly what was said.
He catches every point in a long spoken explanation without needing any of it repeated.
Just from listening, she took in the whole complicated account in one go.
He understood the rambling story perfectly and could hand back the gist straight away.
She listens to a fast talker and never loses a single thread of what they're saying.
He can take in a complicated spoken argument and grasp it without ever seeing it written down.
She got the whole meaning of the speech just from hearing it once.
Tell him a long, layered explanation out loud and he's grasped all of it by the end.
She follows a tangled spoken account effortlessly, however long it runs.
He hears a complicated verbal plan and immediately understands the whole of it.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: The ability to understand speech. Starts with comprehending single words and increases to long complex verbal statements.

narrow_abilities.name: Communication ability
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to use speech to communicate effectively.
seeds: Put her in front of a room and she speaks clearly and confidently, like she was born to it.
He holds his own in any discussion, putting his points across with poise and command.
She can stand up in a meeting and make her point so it lands with everyone there.
He talks to a whole crowd as easily as he talks to one person.
In a group she always gets her ideas across smoothly and brings people around.
When he speaks to a group, he delivers his point so clearly that the whole room follows him.
She can carry a conversation with anyone, in any setting, with real poise.
He addresses the whole room and somehow makes each person feel spoken to directly.
She speaks up in the real moments — interviews, panels — and always comes off composed.
He gets up in front of others and handles the moment with complete composure.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Ability to speak in real-life situations (e.g., lecture, group participation) in an adult-like manner.

narrow_abilities.name: Grammatical sensitivity
narrow_abilities.definition: The awareness of the formal rules of grammar and morphology of words in speech.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs EU (Grw) — sensitivity to grammatical correctness of spoken language, not written punctuation/usage; vs LD.
seeds: She can tell when a spoken sentence comes out grammatically wrong, even if she couldn't name the rule.
He notices the instant a verb doesn't agree with its subject, though he's never studied the rule.
She'll rework a clumsy sentence into the right shape without even thinking about it.
He's got an ear for grammar — wrong tense, a dangling phrase, he catches it.
She just feels when the structure of a sentence is right or off.
She can tell when the wrong word form has been used — a plural where it should be singular, say — just from the grammar.
He's tuned to the grammatical shape of what people say, catching every little slip.
She spots the misplaced word in a sentence that everyone else's ear slid right past.
She can tell a well-formed sentence from a malformed one the moment it's said.
He catches a grammatical slip in someone's speech that everyone else lets slide.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Knowledge or awareness of the grammatical features of the native language.

broad_abilities.name: Domain-specific knowledge
broad_abilities.description: The depth, breadth, and mastery of specialized declarative and procedural knowledge (knowledge not all members of a society are expected to have). The Gkn domain is likely to contain more narrow abilities than are currently listed in the CHC model.

narrow_abilities.name: General science information
narrow_abilities.definition: The range of scientific knowledge (e.g., biology, physics, engineering, mechanics, electronics).
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs K0 (Gc) — specialized science knowledge beyond common general information.
seeds: He always knows the science behind why everyday things happen the way they do.
She can explain how the body fights off an infection without looking anything up.
He knows his physics — why things float, fall, freeze, or fly apart.
She can explain why blood is red or why ice floats, off the top of her head.
He can tell you what's actually going on inside a thunderstorm.
He knows how the planets move and what goes on inside a living cell, all from memory.
He explains the science of cooking, weather, and electricity whenever it comes up.
She carries a wide store of science in her head and can pull up the right fact on the spot.
He knew exactly how vaccines work, and why.
She's the one who knows the real scientific reason, not the myth.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Range of scientific knowledge (e.g., biology, physics, engineering, mechanics, electronics).

narrow_abilities.name: Knowledge of culture
narrow_abilities.definition: The range of knowledge about the humanities (e.g., philosophy, religion, history, literature, music, and art).
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs K1 — the humanities (history, philosophy, religion, literature, music, art), not science; vs K0 (Gc) — specialized depth in the humanities, not the common facts everyone is expected to know.
seeds: My knowledge of history is embarrassingly thin; I mix up which events came first.
I know almost nothing about art or literature, so those conversations go right over my head.
She knows the history of nearly every war, empire, and revolution in far more detail than school ever taught.
He has read so widely in literature and history that he can place almost any book or event in its era.
He picked up an enormous amount of history and literature on his own, far more than any class taught him.
She knows the history behind almost anything, far beyond what we ever covered in school.
I've barely read any classic literature; I don't recognize most of the authors people quote.
She knows art history so well she can name the artist of almost any famous painting.
Play her a few bars of almost any symphony and she'll tell you the composer and the period.
I wish I knew more about history and the arts; I can never follow the references people make to them.

narrow_abilities.name: Mechanical knowledge
narrow_abilities.definition: Knowledge about the function, terminology, and operation of ordinary tools, machines, and equipment.
seeds: He knows what every tool on the bench is called and what each one's for.
She can name the carburetor, the alternator, the timing belt, and tell you what each one does.
He can explain how a combustion engine turns fuel into motion, part by part.
She knows the proper name for that gadget and exactly how it runs.
He can tell you why the gearbox does what it does.
He knew which wrench, which setting, which order, without ever opening a manual.
She understands how a washing machine's drum and pump actually work, right down to the belt.
He talks about pistons and valves like he built them himself.
She knows her way around a workshop — what every tool and part is called and what it's for.
He can name the parts inside a power drill and tell you the job each one does.

narrow_abilities.name: Foreign language proficiency
narrow_abilities.definition: Similar to language development (see Gc) but in another language.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs LD (Gc) — language proficiency specifically in a non-native language.
seeds: After two years abroad she could follow and speak the local language like she'd grown up with it.
He drops into the other language and keeps up with fast native talk without missing a thing.
She reads novels in the foreign language as comfortably as in her own.
He picked up enough of the language to argue, joke, and haggle in it.
She knows the idioms and slang of the other tongue, not just the textbook stuff.
He can hold a deep conversation in his second language without any strain.
She gets complicated ideas across in the foreign language as well as a local would.
He thinks and even dreams in the other language now, the way he once did only in his first.
She handles the fine shades of the foreign language fluently, idioms and all.
He gets by in the other language so naturally people forget it isn't his first.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Similar to Language Development (LD) but for a foreign language.

narrow_abilities.name: Knowledge of signing
narrow_abilities.definition: The knowledge of finger spelling and signing (e.g., American Sign Language).
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs LD/LP — communication through a manual sign modality.
seeds: She signs fluently, her hands carrying whole conversations without a pause.
He can fingerspell a name as fast as someone else would say it out loud.
She caught the entire signed exchange across the room in one glance.
He knows the ASL signs even for unusual words and uses them just right.
She carries on a full, nuanced conversation entirely in sign language.
He reads other people's signing as easily as the rest of us hear speech.
She slips between signing and fingerspelling without breaking mid-sentence.
He's deeply at home in sign language — the grammar, the expression, all of it.
She can follow a whole signed story and understand all of it.
He gets complex ideas across in sign language without ever getting stuck.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Knowledge of finger-spelling and signing (e.g., American Sign Language).

narrow_abilities.name: Skill in lip reading
narrow_abilities.definition: Competence in the ability to understand communication from others by watching the movement of their mouths and expressions.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs LS — extracting speech content from lip movements with no audio.
seeds: She can follow what you're saying across a noisy room just by watching your lips.
He followed the whole conversation with the sound off, reading it from their lips alone.
Even with the TV muted she can tell what the actors are saying.
He reads lips so well he barely needs to hear you at all.
She caught what they were whispering just from the shape of their mouths.
He can pick the words off people's lips from clear across the street.
She follows a speaker by the movement of their lips the second the audio cuts.
She read the words straight off my lips even though she couldn't hear a thing I said.
With no sound to go on, she works out what's being said purely from how the lips move.
He pieces speech together from lips alone, no sound required.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Competence in the ability to understand communication from others by watching the movements of their mouths and expressions.

broad_abilities.name: Quantitative knowledge
broad_abilities.description: The depth and breadth of declarative and procedural knowledge related to mathematics. The Gq domain is likely to contain more narrow abilities than are currently listed in the CHC model.

narrow_abilities.name: Mathematical knowledge
narrow_abilities.definition: The range of general knowledge, not performance of mathematic operations or the solving of problems.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs RQ (Gf) — knows math concepts/terms/rules (knowing-that); vs A3 — knowledge, not demonstrated performance; vs N — knowing, not speed.
seeds: He knows his way around the ideas of math — what the terms mean and which rule applies where.
She can name and explain the formulas long after she last had any use for them.
He knows which method is the one that fits which kind of problem.
She's got a broad store of mathematical facts and rules in her head.
He knows what each mathematical rule is for, even ones he hasn't used in years.
She can tell you what a mathematical term means in plain words, off the top of her head.
He knows the names and meanings of the operations and symbols.
She's got a wide store of math knowledge in her head, the kind you'd want on a quiz team.
He recalls the rules of algebra without any effort.
She knows the names and meanings of the rules cold, though she rarely sits down to use them.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Range of general knowledge about mathematics.

narrow_abilities.name: Mathematical achievement
narrow_abilities.definition: Measured (tested) mathematics achievement.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs KM — demonstrated skill at actually doing/solving mathematics correctly (doing), not knowing about it; vs N — accuracy of full procedures, not raw speed.
seeds: He aces every math exam, working each problem right from start to finish.
She doesn't just know the math — she can sit down and actually do it, right, every time.
He carries out the long multi-step procedures without dropping a step or slipping up.
She always comes back with the right answer in math class, whatever's on the board.
He puts the right method to work and lands on the correct answer.
She works the calculations all the way through and lands on the correct result.
He gets top marks in maths, getting the working and the answers correct every time.
She runs the procedures cleanly — the working checks out and so does the answer.
When the math test comes, she's the one who scores full marks, every procedure done correctly.
Whatever the math task, she finishes it accurately and in full.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Measured mathematics achievement.

broad_abilities.name: Reading and writing
broad_abilities.description: The depth and breadth of declarative and procedural knowledge and skills related to written language.

narrow_abilities.name: Reading comprehension
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to understand written discourse.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs RD — understanding the meaning of written text, not decoding; vs LS — written, not spoken.
seeds: She reads a dense chapter and comes away understanding every argument in it.
He grasps exactly what a passage means, not just the words sitting on the page.
She reads a dense article and can lay out for you exactly what it claims and why.
He understood the whole story's meaning, including the parts only hinted at.
She follows a long written explanation and holds onto the full sense of it.
He reads a complicated passage and comes away with the deeper point, not just the surface.
She takes in a difficult chapter and understands the whole of it as she reads.
He can tell you what an article really argued after a single read.
She pulls the meaning out of dense writing without any effort.
He reads connected text and sees how all the parts fit together.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Ability to comprehend connected discourse during reading.

narrow_abilities.name: Reading decoding
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to identify words from text.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs RC — turning print into spoken words incl. nonwords (decoding), not understanding meaning; vs PC (Ga) — print, not oral phoneme manipulation.
seeds: She can sound out any word on the page, even ones she's never come across, reading it letter by letter.
He reads unfamiliar names and made-up words aloud without stumbling.
She works through long, tricky words smoothly, sounding out one letter-chunk at a time.
He can read a nonsense word aloud correctly just from how it's spelled.
If he's never seen the word written before, he can't work out what it is — he can't sound it out at all.
He turns the printed letters into the right sounds automatically.
He reads familiar words on sight and sounds out the rest with ease.
She read the unpronounceable street names straight off, no trouble.
She can read a word she's never seen before, building it up from its letters and sounds.
He'll read made-up names and nonsense words aloud accurately — his sounding-out is that solid.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Ability to recognize and decode words or pseudowords in reading.

narrow_abilities.name: Reading speed
narrow_abilities.definition: The rate at which a person can read connected discourse with full comprehension.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs RC — speed, not depth.
seeds: She reads a page in seconds, moving down it far faster than anyone else.
He reads several times faster than anyone else around him.
She'd finished the whole report in the time it took us to get through the summary.
His eyes fly down the page; he's done before you've even started.
She can get through a long article in a couple of minutes flat.
He gets through text at a pace that seems impossible, eyes racing down each page.
She turns pages so fast you'd swear she was only skimming.
He gets through the assigned chapters in a fraction of the time.
She reads silently at a flat-out pace and never slows down.
He blew through the dense manual far quicker than the rest of us.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Time required to silently read a passage or series of sentences as quickly as possible.

narrow_abilities.name: Writing ability
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to use written text to communicate ideas clearly.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs EU — quality of written expression (clarity, organization, structure), not mechanics; vs WS — quality, not speed.
seeds: She writes with such clarity that complicated ideas come out feeling simple.
He sets a piece up so every paragraph flows logically into the next.
Her prose is well-organized and a pleasure to read, each thought set out in order.
He can take a tangle of half-formed thoughts and lay them out in clear prose.
She arranges her writing so the point builds naturally from start to finish.
His writing is so well-organized you never once lose the thread.
She gets herself across on the page with real clarity and order.
He crafts sentences that are tight, clear, and well-made.
Her written work is a model of organization and solid structure.
He writes the way a good architect builds — everything set in its place.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Ability to write with clarity of thought, organization, and good sentence structure. (Not clearly defined by existing research.)

narrow_abilities.name: Spelling ability
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to spell words.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs EU — producing correct spelling specifically, not broader punctuation/usage.
seeds: She can spell anything — the long ones, the weird ones, all of them right.
He spells so phonetically that he misspells almost everything — 'enuff,' 'becuase,' the lot.
She spells the trickiest words without a flicker of doubt.
Words like 'loose' and 'lose' she can never spell right, no matter how often she's corrected.
She never makes a spelling slip, even in a rushed text.
He spells unfamiliar words right, no autocorrect needed.
She's a flawless speller — the one you ask when you're not sure.
He nails the spelling of words most people get wrong.
She can rattle off the correct spelling of nearly anything you throw at her.
His spelling is spotless, no autocorrect required.
narrow_abilities.prior_definition: Ability to spell. (Not clearly defined by existing research.)

narrow_abilities.name: Writing speed
narrow_abilities.definition: The ability to copy or generate text quickly.
narrow_abilities.discriminator: vs WA — speed of producing/copying text, not quality.
seeds: She fills a page with her own writing in the time it takes most people to begin.
He gets his own thoughts down on paper faster than the rest of us can think them.
Her pen flies as her own words pour straight onto the page.
He can write out a long passage of his own in a fraction of the usual time.
She gets her own ideas down in writing at remarkable speed.
He produces a full page of his own writing before anyone else has a paragraph.
She writes her own text so fast her hand barely keeps up.
He gets the whole thing written out as fast as the words come to him.
She turns out her own written work quickly without ever slowing.
His writing speed lets him finish a written exam, in his own words, with time to spare.
